assumptions: The report's memory model requires every quantum register that persists across a counted round to undergo that round's stated noise. It allows ideal joint controls, measurements, resets, fresh unentangled ancillas, classical randomness, and classical feed-forward.

The memory model excludes a noiseless quantum bypass, access to environmental error labels, operations on the reference, and uncounted entanglement; success probability includes the encoder and every selected event.

The width classification is stated for a fixed CPTP channel with positive-definite Choi matrix and conditions on distillability of J(Phi)/d. The variable-stopping theorem assumes each whole-memory noise layer has the stated k-broadcastability property and uses fidelity conditions at each nonempty success-time bin.

contract.interface: The report states an earlier broadcasting-based fixed-deadline success bound, a distillability-dependent sharp-order width classification, a finite exact lifetime at fixed width under full-rank noise, a cumulative variable-width resource law, and a variable-stopping-time inequality. For the stopping theorem, q is reference dimension, k is broadcast multiplicity, and p_n,F_n are success probability and conditional Bell fidelity at time n; the report states sum_n k^n p_n(q F_n - 1)_+ <= q - 1. For qubits with F_n >= 1-epsilon at every nonempty success-time bin, it states E[k^tau 1_success] <= 1/(1-2 epsilon).
